lead: Valencia is not only sustainable: it is smart. European Green Capital 2024 and European Capital of Smart Tourism 2022, the city combines technology, nature and culture to offer a responsible, accessible travel experience with no unnecessary impact.

Valencia is much more than a pretty destination: it is a city that has made sustainability and technology the axes of its urban management. Being a smart tourist in Valencia is easy, because the city is already designed for it: you can get around without a car, drink free filtered tap water on any street, connect to the internet without using data and travel to the Albufera without leaving a carbon footprint.
These are the smart and sustainable initiatives you will be able to experience during your visit without even looking for them.

items.title: Green mobility
items.body: Bikes, scooters, clean public transport and zero cars in the historic centre.

items.title: Accessible technology
items.body: Free WiFi, transport apps and systems for people with visual impairments.

items.title: Protected nature
items.body: Albufera, huerta, marine Posidonia and more than 500 catalogued monumental trees.

items.title: Circular economy
items.body: Composting, oil recycling, neighbourhood markets and kilometre 0.

items.title: Renewable energy
items.body: Solar panels on municipal buildings, hydrogen at the port and wave energy.

items.title: Citizen participation
items.body: More than 150 businesses signed up to the Green Pact and environmental education programmes.

items.title: PUSDAR filtered water fountains
items.body: More than 50 filtered, chilled tap water fountains spread across the city. Instead of buying bottled water, you can refill your own bottle free of charge at any of these points. The PUSDAR network eliminates thousands of plastic bottles a year and offers water of the same or better quality than bottled.

items.title: Free public WiFi · WiFi4EU
items.body: More than 400 public, free, high-speed WiFi access points spread across the whole city. The network is part of the European Union’s WiFi4EU programme and offers 30 Mbps at each point. Available in squares, gardens, beaches, museums and municipal buildings.

items.title: Hybrid and electric buses · EMT
items.body: The fleet of urban buses of EMT Valencia includes hybrid vehicles with which the carbon footprint of urban transport has been reduced by 22%. The addition of new 100% electric vehicles, with absolutely no CO2 emissions, strengthens the city’s commitment to clean urban mobility.
facts: 22% reduction in carbon footprint · New electric buses

items.title: Smart bus stops · Navilens
items.body: The new bus-stop shelters feature Navilens technology to guide people with visual impairments through a smartphone app. They also include Braille plates, free WiFi access and USB ports for charging your phone. A system that makes public transport more accessible and smarter.

items.title: Bike and boat tours · Easy Albufera Bike & Boat
items.body: The range of bike tours around Valencia and its surroundings grows every year. The Easy Albufera Bike & Boat tour combines cycling to the Albufera with a boat trip on the lake: zero emissions, with a local guide and in direct contact with the two most emblematic ecosystems around Valencia.
facts: Complete zero-emission tour · Bike + boat · Local guide

items.title: Smart pedestrian crossings · Marina
items.body: The first smart pedestrian crossings in the city have been installed at the Marina de Valencia, fitted with sensors and LED technology that lights up as soon as a pedestrian approaches, to warn vehicles in good time. A system that improves road safety and reduces the risk of accidents in the areas with the most pedestrian traffic.
facts: Sensors · Smart LED · Greater pedestrian safety

items.title: Sustainable street furniture · Marina and beaches
items.body: The new street-furniture structures at the Marina and the beaches are made from rice husk, recycled materials and Posidonia oceanica leaves washed up by the tide. A resistant, sustainable design inspired by ceramic mosaics and the waves of the sea. Art, functionality and respect for the environment in a single object.

items.title: Wave Energy Converter · Wave energy
items.body: The waves of the Mediterranean are harnessed to generate green energy in Valencia thanks to the Wave Energy Converter, a device installed at the mouth of the Marina canal. A pioneering project in Spain that converts the kinetic energy of the sea into clean electricity, reducing dependence on fossil fuels in running the marina.
facts: Marina canal · Wave energy · Pioneering project

blocks.title: Smart Valencia · What you need to know before you arrive
items: Tap water in Valencia is drinkable: the PUSDAR fountains filter and chill it for free
There are more than 400 free WiFi points across the city: squares, gardens, beaches and museums
EMT buses have cut their carbon footprint by 22% with a hybrid fleet
The Port of Valencia is the first in Europe to use hydrogen to reduce emissions
Bus stops have Navilens technology for people with visual impairments
Valencia was the first city in the world to certify its tourism carbon footprint
